Q1: Where should the step durations come from to choose which steps leave `tests-release-and-log-analysis`?
Choices:
A) The implementer times each step's own test command in its sandbox (for example `time python3 tests/<file>`). It moves the slowest steps, as written, until the job's measured total is under 75% of its 20 minutes (the `budget-watch` warning ratio, about 15 minutes). The measured times go in the PR description. (RECOMMENDED)
B) An operator posts the per-step durations from run 39030079651 as an `/answer`, and the plan moves steps using those exact numbers.
C) No timing at all: move a fixed set of the steps that look heaviest (the inline "Release CI gate tests (stubbed gh; both release workflows)" block, the three workflow-log coverage gates and "Validation harness sandbox tests").
Q2: Which job may receive the moved steps?
Choices:
A) Exactly one of the other three test jobs (`tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`, `tests-promote-stall-and-review`): the one with the lowest measured total, as long as it also stays under 75% of its 20 minutes after the move. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Split the moved steps across two or more of those three test jobs, so each one stays under 75%.
C) A or B, and `static-checks` (15-minute budget) may also receive steps.
**Note:** the `orchestrate-poll` matrix job is never a target under any choice. A step moved there would run once per matrix group.
